accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the formation of the Indian and American federations?
o: India followed a holding-together model, whereas the USA followed a coming-together model
India followed a coming-together model, whereas the USA followed a holding-together model
Both India and the USA followed a coming-together model
Both India and the USA followed a holding-together model
accepted.x: India is a holding-together federation in which a large country distributes power among units to preserve unity. The USA is a coming-together federation formed when independent States agreed to unite.
accepted.tq: Test the central distinction between holding-together and coming-together federations.
accepted.sec: India vs USA federal systems - common and differing features (citizenship, lists, judiciary)

accepted.s: With reference to citizenship in India and the USA, which of the following is correct?
o: India provides for single citizenship, whereas the USA provides for dual citizenship
India provides for dual citizenship, whereas the USA provides for single citizenship
Both India and the USA provide only for single citizenship
Both India and the USA provide only for dual citizenship
accepted.x: India has single citizenship. The USA follows a dual citizenship arrangement involving the Union and the State.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the closely related single-citizenship and dual-citizenship models.
accepted.sec: India vs USA federal systems - common and differing features (citizenship, lists, judiciary)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the distribution of legislative powers in India and the USA:
1. India has three legislative lists in the Constitution.
2. In India, residuary powers are vested in the Centre.
3. In the USA, residuary powers are vested in the States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: India has the Union, State and Concurrent Lists, and residuary powers belong to the Centre. In the USA, only federal powers are enumerated and residuary powers remain with the States.
accepted.tq: Split the options by checking the allocation of residuary powers in each federation.
accepted.sec: India vs USA federal systems - common and differing features (citizenship, lists, judiciary)

accepted.s: The judicial structure of the United States differs from that of India in that the United States has
o: separate federal and State court systems
only State courts and no federal courts
no system of judicial review
a single integrated judiciary for the Union and the States
accepted.x: India has a single integrated judiciary, whereas the USA maintains separate federal and State court systems.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional contrast between an integrated judiciary and dual court systems.
accepted.sec: India vs USA federal systems - common and differing features (citizenship, lists, judiciary)

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes India from the United States regarding State constitutions?
o: Indian States generally do not have separate constitutions, whereas each American State has its own constitution
Only the former State of Jammu and Kashmir had a constitution in the United States
Every Indian State has a separate constitution, while no American State has one
Neither Indian nor American States have separate constitutions
accepted.x: Indian States generally do not possess separate constitutions; the former Jammu and Kashmir was an exception. Each State of the USA has its own constitution.
accepted.tq: Watch for the exception embedded in the State-constitution comparison.
accepted.sec: India vs USA federal systems - common and differing features (citizenship, lists, judiciary)

accepted.s: In relation to the upper chambers of the Indian and American legislatures, which of the following is correct?
o: India gives every State two seats, whereas the USA allocates Senate seats by population
India broadly allocates representation by population, whereas every American State has two seats in the Senate
Both allocate seats equally among their constituent units
Neither country has an upper chamber based on representation of constituent units
accepted.x: Representation in India's Rajya Sabha is broadly linked to population. In the USA, each State has equal representation of two Senators.
accepted.tq: Compare the population-based and equal-representation principles in the two upper Houses.
accepted.sec: India vs USA federal systems - common and differing features (citizenship, lists, judiciary)

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: India — dual citizenship and State constitutions
USA — three legislative lists and residuary powers with the Centre
India — single citizenship and a single integrated judiciary
USA — upper House seats allocated according to population of States
accepted.x: India has single citizenship and a single integrated judicial system. The other pairs reverse the constitutional features of India and the USA.
accepted.tq: Reject options that swap institutional features between the two federations.
accepted.sec: India vs USA federal systems - common and differing features (citizenship, lists, judiciary)

accepted.s: During which period was federalism in India characterised by Congress dominance, with conflicts generally settled within the party and the system remaining cooperative but centralised?
accepted.x: The period from 1952 to 1967 was marked by Congress dominance. Federal relations were cooperative but centralised because many conflicts were resolved within the ruling party.
accepted.tq: Link the political-party phase with its characteristic pattern of Centre-State relations.
accepted.sec: Federal practice over time - phases of centralisation and decentralisation by decade

accepted.s: The Rajamannar Committee was associated with which phase of federal practice in India?
o: 1967-1977, when non-Congress State governments generated confrontation with the Centre
1952-1967, when Congress dominance prevailed
1977-1989, when the Sarkaria Commission was appointed
1989-2014, when coalition governments strengthened negotiated federalism
accepted.x: The Rajamannar Committee was set up in 1969 during the phase from 1967 to 1977, when non-Congress State governments led to greater Centre-State confrontation. Re-centralisation continued up to the Emergency of 1975.
accepted.tq: Use the date of the committee to place it in the correct federal phase.
accepted.sec: Federal practice over time - phases of centralisation and decentralisation by decade

accepted.s: Which of the following developments is associated with the period 1977-1989 in Centre-State relations?
o: The appointment of the Sarkaria Commission in 1983
The replacement of the Planning Commission by NITI Aayog in 2015
The appointment of the Rajamannar Committee in 1969
The establishment of the Inter-State Council in 1990
accepted.x: The Sarkaria Commission was appointed in 1983, falling within the 1977-1989 phase. The other developments belong to different periods.
accepted.tq: Match the named institutional development with its correct time period.
accepted.sec: Federal practice over time - phases of centralisation and decentralisation by decade

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the coalition era of Indian federalism:
1. It broadly extended from 1989 to 2014.
2. Regional parties acquired greater bargaining power.
3. The Inter-State Council was set up in 1990.
4. The S.R. Bommai judgment of 1994 placed limits on the use of Article 356.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: All four statements describe important features of the 1989-2014 coalition phase. Federalism became more genuinely negotiated, the Inter-State Council was set up in 1990, and S.R. Bommai limited arbitrary use of Article 356.
accepted.tq: Verify the period first and then connect the institutions and judgment associated with it.
accepted.sec: Federal practice over time - phases of centralisation and decentralisation by decade

accepted.s: The expression “cooperative-competitive federalism” is particularly associated with the period beginning in 2014 because
o: the Inter-State Council was established and the Sarkaria Commission was appointed
Congress dominance ended and the S.R. Bommai judgment was delivered
the Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015 and GST was introduced in 2017
the Rajamannar Committee was appointed and the Emergency was proclaimed
accepted.x: From 2014 onward, NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission in 2015 and GST was introduced in 2017, within the framework described as cooperative-competitive federalism.
accepted.tq: Identify the phase through its two distinctive institutional and fiscal developments.
accepted.sec: Federal practice over time - phases of centralisation and decentralisation by decade

accepted.s:
Arrange the following phases of Indian federal practice in chronological order:
A. Coalition era and more negotiated federalism
B. Congress dominance with centralised cooperation
C. Non-Congress State governments and Centre-State confrontation
D. Janata interlude followed by the return of Congress
o: B, C, D, A
C, B, D, A
B, D, C, A
D, B, C, A
accepted.x: The correct sequence is 1952-1967, 1967-1977, 1977-1989 and 1989-2014. These correspond respectively to B, C, D and A.
accepted.tq: Fix the first phase and then place the committee and coalition phases by their dates.
accepted.sec: Federal practice over time - phases of centralisation and decentralisation by decade

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Sarkaria Commission — 1983
Inter-State Council — 1990
Rajamannar Committee — 1969
accepted.x: GST arrived in 2017, not 2015. NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission in 2015, while the other three pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the one shifted year among a set of correctly dated federal developments.
accepted.sec: Federal practice over time - phases of centralisation and decentralisation by decade

accepted.s: Which of the following countries represents a coming-together federation?
o: India
Belgium
Spain
Switzerland
accepted.x: Switzerland is a coming-together federation in which independent States or units pool sovereignty while retaining equal power. India, Spain and Belgium are examples of holding-together federations.
accepted.tq: Separate examples of the two federation types rather than relying only on their definitions.
accepted.sec: Holding-together vs coming-together federations

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. In a coming-together federation, independent States pool sovereignty and retain equal power.
2. A holding-together federation generally has a stronger Centre.
3. India, Spain and Belgium are examples of holding-together federations.
4. The USA, Switzerland and Australia are examples of coming-together federations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe the two types of federation and their examples. Coming-together federations preserve greater equality among the constituent units, while holding-together federations usually retain a stronger Centre.
accepted.tq: Check both the defining characteristics and the complete example lists.
accepted.sec: Holding-together vs coming-together federations

accepted.s: The formation of India's federation is described by the Centre for the Study of Developing Societies as having occurred through
o: replacement of a confederation by a unitary State
equal secession of sovereign States
disintegration, in contrast to integration in the USA
integration, in contrast to disintegration in the USA
accepted.x: India's federation is described as formed by “disintegration”, meaning division of power within a large country. The US federation is described as formed by “integration” of independent States.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the easily reversed terms integration and disintegration.
accepted.sec: Holding-together vs coming-together federations

accepted.s: Which of the following was a feature of Article 370 before it was made inoperative?
o: The State of Jammu and Kashmir had a separate constitution and flag
All Union laws automatically applied without State concurrence
The Directive Principles of State Policy were made compulsory in the State
Financial Emergency provisions were expressly applicable to the State
accepted.x: Article 370 provided Jammu and Kashmir with a separate constitution and flag. It also required State concurrence for the application of certain Union laws, while Financial Emergency and the Directive Principles were not applicable in the stated manner.
accepted.tq: Identify the authentic special provision while rejecting reversed constitutional effects.
accepted.sec: Asymmetric federalism - Article 370 (former), Article 371 series, Fifth and Sixth Schedules

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the former Article 370 arrangement:
1. Certain Union laws required the concurrence of the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
2. The State had a separate constitution and flag.
3. The provisions were made inoperative in August 2019.
4. The Supreme Court upheld this action in December 2023.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Article 370 provided the special arrangements, which were made inoperative in August 2019; the Supreme Court upheld the action in December 2023.
accepted.tq: Track the provision, its constitutional change and the subsequent judicial validation in sequence.
accepted.sec: Asymmetric federalism - Article 370 (former), Article 371 series, Fifth and Sixth Schedules

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with the subject of the Article 371 series?
o: Article 371D — special provisions for Andhra Pradesh
Article 371 — autonomous district councils in Mizoram
Article 371A — special provisions for Goa alone
Article 371J — special provisions for Sikkim
accepted.x: Article 371D provides special provisions for Andhra Pradesh. The Article 371 series also covers Maharashtra and Gujarat, North-Eastern States, Sikkim, Goa and Karnataka through different provisions.
accepted.tq: Match the specific article to the State without confusing it with the Fifth or Sixth Schedule.
accepted.sec: Asymmetric federalism - Article 370 (former), Article 371 series, Fifth and Sixth Schedules

accepted.s: The range of constitutional provisions dealing with special arrangements for States under the Article 371 series is
o: Articles 371 to 371J
Articles 370 to 371C
Articles 350 to 360
Articles 372 to 380
accepted.x: The special provisions referred to in the Article 371 series extend from Article 371 to Article 371J. They cover several States and regions, including Maharashtra, Gujarat, the North-Eastern States, Sikkim, Goa, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Use the exact article range to avoid confusing the 370 provision with the 371 series.
accepted.sec: Asymmetric federalism - Article 370 (former), Article 371 series, Fifth and Sixth Schedules

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Fifth Schedule from the Sixth Schedule?
o: The Fifth Schedule concerns financial emergencies, while the Sixth Schedule concerns the Union List
The Fifth Schedule provides for autonomous district councils, while the Sixth Schedule deals only with Scheduled Areas
The Fifth Schedule deals with Scheduled Areas, while the Sixth Schedule provides for autonomous district councils
Both Schedules deal exclusively with the administration of Jammu and Kashmir
accepted.x: The Fifth Schedule provides for the administration and control of Scheduled Areas. The Sixth Schedule establishes autonomous district councils in specified North-Eastern areas.
accepted.tq: Separate the two Schedules by their institutional purpose.
accepted.sec: Asymmetric federalism - Article 370 (former), Article 371 series, Fifth and Sixth Schedules

accepted.s: Autonomous district councils under the Sixth Schedule are provided for in which group of States?
o: Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh
Maharashtra, Gujarat, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh
Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram
Nagaland, Manipur, Sikkim and Goa
accepted.x: The Sixth Schedule provides for autonomous district councils in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
accepted.tq: Recall the complete State group attached to the Sixth Schedule.
accepted.sec: Asymmetric federalism - Article 370 (former), Article 371 series, Fifth and Sixth Schedules

accepted.s: A constitutional provision specifically intended for the administration of Scheduled Areas would be found in the
o: Fourth Schedule
Ninth Schedule
Fifth Schedule
Sixth Schedule
accepted.x: The Fifth Schedule deals with the administration of Scheduled Areas. The Sixth Schedule, by contrast, concerns autonomous district councils in specified North-Eastern States.
accepted.tq: Apply the purpose of each Schedule to a short administrative situation.
accepted.sec: Asymmetric federalism - Article 370 (former), Article 371 series, Fifth and Sixth Schedules

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the correct classification of the United States and India respectively?
o: United States — holding-together federation; India — coming-together federation
United States — coming-together federation; India — holding-together federation
Both — holding-together federations
Both — coming-together federations
accepted.x: The USA is a coming-together federation formed by the union of independent States. India is a holding-together federation designed to preserve unity in a diverse country through distribution of powers.
accepted.tq: Test the paired classification without reversing the two federation models.
accepted.sec: Holding-together vs coming-together federations

accepted.s: Which of the following developments marked the transition from the coalition phase to the phase beginning in 2014?
o: The replacement of the Planning Commission by NITI Aayog in 2015
The establishment of the Inter-State Council in 1990
The appointment of the Sarkaria Commission in 1983
The appointment of the Rajamannar Committee in 1969
accepted.x: The phase beginning in 2014 is associated with NITI Aayog replacing the Planning Commission in 2015. The other developments belong to earlier phases of federal practice.
accepted.tq: Identify the latest phase through its defining institutional change.
accepted.sec: Federal practice over time - phases of centralisation and decentralisation by decade
